title: Napoleonic era ends at Waterloo
text: The technology reading uses Waterloo as a reference point for comparing nineteenth-century warfare with WWI.

title: Crimean War
text: A background example in the readings of European conflict before the much larger industrial war of 1914.

title: American Civil War
text: The technology feature links earlier ironclads and large-scale warfare to later developments.
note: The photograph prints 1860–1865; the war began in 1861.

title: Franco-Prussian War
text: Prussia and its allies defeat France. The conflict helps bring about German unification and French resentment over lost territory.

title: German unification; Alsace-Lorraine changes hands
text: A powerful unified Germany alters Europe’s balance of power. France’s loss of Alsace-Lorraine contributes to a lasting rivalry.

title: First Ottoman constitution
text: The Young Turks later demand restoration of constitutional government as part of their challenge to Ottoman autocracy.
note: The constitution was promulgated in 1876; its suspension belongs to 1878, despite the reading’s compressed wording.

title: Triple Alliance forms
text: Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy form the prewar alliance. Italy’s wartime choice later differs from this alignment.

title: Indian National Congress founded
text: The nationalist organization predates the Paris Peace Conference by decades.
note: Included to clarify the handout’s misleading description of a “newly created” Congress in 1919.

title: Franco-Russian alliance takes shape
text: Military arrangements connect France and Russia, increasing Germany’s fear of fighting on two fronts.

title: German seizure and lease at Jiaozhou
text: German rights in Shandong later become the subject of competing Japanese and Chinese claims at Paris.
note: The German occupation began in 1897; the lease agreement followed in 1898.

title: Hague declaration addresses asphyxiating gas
text: International restrictions did not prevent the later development and use of chemical weapons.

title: Boxer uprising in China
text: The chronology table places the uprising in the wider crisis of the imperial order.

title: Anglo-Japanese alliance
text: The alliance diagram shows a relationship extending the European diplomatic system into East Asia.

title: Britain and France reach an entente
text: Their diplomatic understanding helps form the alignments that later become the Triple Entente.

title: Russo-Japanese War
text: Japan defeats Russia, demonstrating changes in military and imperial power beyond western Europe.

title: Britain and Russia reach an entente
text: Together with the Franco-Russian and Anglo-French relationships, this completes the core Triple Entente alignment.

title: Hague Convention on land warfare
text: The technology reading connects restrictions on poison weapons with their later violation during WWI.

title: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia-Herzegovina
text: The annexation frustrates Serbian nationalist ambitions and sharpens tensions in the Balkans.

title: Young Turks depose Abdul Hamid II
text: Reform and modernization proceed alongside centralization and policies that alienate minorities.

title: Chinese revolution challenges Qing rule
text: The reading’s chronology identifies the revolution associated with Sun Yat-sen; the Qing dynasty formally ends in 1912.

title: Italy conquers Ottoman Libya
text: The loss of Libya illustrates the erosion of Ottoman territory and European imperial competition.

title: Balkan Wars
text: Balkan states fight over Ottoman lands and the regional settlement. Most Ottoman European territory is lost.

title: Albania declares independence
text: A national independence claim forms part of the Ottoman retreat from the Balkans.
note: The textbook’s 1910 reference should not be memorized as the independence date.

title: Assassination in Sarajevo
text: Gavrilo Princip kills Franz Ferdinand and his wife. The assassination triggers the July Crisis.

title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
text: The regional crisis becomes an open war and activates fears and commitments among the larger powers.

title: Russian mobilization escalates the crisis
text: Russian support for Serbia and military preparations intensify German fears of a wider conflict.
note: Partial mobilization was ordered on July 29; general mobilization followed on July 30.

title: Germany declares war on Russia
text: The crisis now directly involves two major powers and their partners.

title: Germany declares war on France
text: Germany’s strategy aims for a fast western victory before a prolonged struggle against Russia.

title: Germany invades Belgium; Britain enters
text: The invasion of neutral Belgium helps bring Britain into the war against Germany.
note: The reading places entry into Belgium on August 3; August 4 is the invasion date used here.

title: Japan takes German positions in China
text: Japan’s wartime occupation becomes a basis for its Shandong claims at the peace conference.

title: First Battle of the Marne
text: Allied resistance helps halt the German advance near Paris. The planned quick victory fails.

title: Western Front trench system develops
text: Opposing armies establish connected defenses from the North Sea to the Swiss border.

title: Ottoman Empire enters the war
text: Ottoman participation alongside the Central Powers expands the conflict into additional theaters.

title: Japan presents the Twenty-One Demands
text: The demands seek expanded Japanese influence in China and frame later Chinese objections at Paris.

title: Large-scale chlorine-gas warfare on the Western Front
text: Chemical warfare adds terror and suffering; other belligerents also use gas.
note: Britain used gas in 1915, despite the technology box’s later date.

title: ANZAC landing at Gallipoli
text: The Allied campaign against Ottoman defenses becomes central to Australian and New Zealand wartime memory.

title: Treaty of London; Italy joins the Allies
text: Territorial promises help draw Italy to the Allied side. Italy declares war on Austria-Hungary in May.

title: Lusitania is sunk
text: The loss of the passenger liner generates anger and U.S. protests but does not bring immediate U.S. entry.

title: Battle of Verdun
text: A long and costly battle exemplifies attrition and the limits of industrial offensives.

title: Battle of Jutland
text: The major British-German surface-fleet engagement does not end Britain’s strategic blockade.

title: Arab Revolt; competing wartime promises
text: Arab revolt against Ottoman rule is encouraged by expectations of independence. British-French arrangements complicate those expectations.

title: Battle of the Somme
text: Huge losses accompany limited advances. British tanks make their battlefield debut during the campaign.

title: Romania enters the war on the Allied side
text: Romania later invokes its agreement with the Entente and its wartime sacrifices to support territorial claims.

title: Germany’s “turnip winter”
text: Blockade, food shortages, and a failed potato harvest worsen civilian hardship.

title: Zimmermann Telegram
text: Germany proposes Mexican cooperation in a possible war with the United States, offering support for recovery of Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona.

title: Unrestricted submarine warfare resumes
text: Germany hopes to defeat Britain before American intervention becomes decisive.

title: Russian revolutions
text: War losses and hardship help destabilize the Russian state. Revolution changes its government and its role in the war.

title: United States declares war on Germany
text: Congress declares war after Wilson’s request, amid submarine warfare and other pressures.
note: Wilson requested war on April 2; April 6 is the declaration date.

title: Brazil enters WWI
text: German attacks on merchant shipping and ties to the United States help shape Brazil’s participation and postwar aims.

title: Balfour Declaration
text: Britain supports a Jewish national home in Palestine, with language concerning existing communities’ civil and religious rights.
note: The declaration dates to 1917, not the 1916 date printed in the conference handout.

title: Bolsheviks seize power
text: Lenin’s movement takes control as Russia’s war effort and political order break down.
note: Often called the October Revolution because Russia then used a different calendar.

title: Russian Civil War
text: The Bolsheviks fight anti-communist forces; warfare, economic collapse, and famine follow. The main struggle described in the reading centers on 1918–1921.
note: The reading’s December 1918 opening is too narrow for the full civil-war period. This range overlaps the final phase of WWI.

title: Wilson presents the Fourteen Points
text: The program outlines principles for peace, including territorial settlement and an association of nations.

title: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
text: The Bolshevik government ends Russia’s participation in the war, accepting major territorial losses.

title: German offensives in the west
text: Ludendorff seeks victory before the growing American presence becomes overwhelming, but the offensives do not secure a decisive win.

title: Allied counterattacks force German retreat
text: Allied pressure, growing American strength, and German exhaustion reverse the momentum.

title: German leadership and military morale break down
text: Ludendorff resigns and naval mutinies accompany wider unrest, weakening the capacity to keep fighting.

title: Armistice takes effect
text: Fighting on the Western Front stops. A final peace treaty still has to be negotiated.

title: Influenza pandemic in the readings
text: Global movement, wartime conditions, and limited medical tools help a devastating pandemic spread.
note: The pandemic extended beyond these two years in wider historical accounts. The uploaded page also contains conflicting death estimates.

title: Paris Peace Conference
text: Victors negotiate treaties amid competing security, territorial, economic, and national demands.

title: Racial-equality proposal and Pan-African organizing
text: Japan proposes an equality provision; Pan-African advocates seek legal protections and participation in government. The conference does not fulfill these demands.

title: Korean independence protests
text: The March First Movement protests Japanese rule. Unofficial Korean representatives seek a hearing at Paris.

title: Amritsar massacre
text: British repression deepens Indian anger and challenges imperial claims to liberal values.

title: May Fourth Movement in China
text: The transfer of German Shandong rights to Japan provokes protests over sovereignty and the peace settlement.

title: Vietnamese eight-point petition
text: Nguyễn Ái Quốc, later known as Ho Chi Minh, petitions for civil rights, legal reforms, and representation under French rule.

title: Treaty of Versailles signed
text: Germany signs the treaty containing territorial changes, military limits, reparations, and a responsibility clause.

title: Greco-Turkish conflict and Turkish nationalist struggle
text: Turkish nationalists resist postwar territorial arrangements and foreign occupation, leading to a revised settlement.

title: New Economic Policy begins
text: Lenin allows limited private enterprise to revive the devastated economy while retaining Communist rule and control of major sectors.
note: The uploaded textbook prints 1923. The accepted start date is 1921.

title: United States makes separate peace treaties
text: After rejecting ratification of Versailles, the United States concludes separate peace agreements with Germany, Austria, and Hungary.

title: U.S. immigration restrictions
text: Quota laws limit immigration, including arrivals from eastern and southern Europe, during a period of displacement.

title: Shandong settlement restores Chinese sovereignty
text: The settlement revisits Japan’s gains of 1919 and restores Chinese sovereignty in Shandong.

title: Egypt gains nominal independence
text: The reading’s chronology places limited Egyptian independence within the wider postwar Middle Eastern changes.

title: German-Soviet rapprochement and cooperation
text: Germany and Soviet Russia cooperate outside parts of the Versailles framework, including military and industrial links.

title: Soviet Union formed
text: A new union consolidates Bolshevik control over much of the former tsarist empire, while several neighboring states remain independent.

title: Ruhr occupation and German hyperinflation
text: The reparations crisis, foreign occupation, and monetary expansion intensify economic and political instability.

title: Revised Turkish settlement and republic
text: The Treaty of Lausanne recognizes a revised settlement; the Republic of Turkey is proclaimed later in the year.

title: Lenin dies; succession struggle intensifies
text: Stalin and Trotsky become central rivals, with party organization and competing visions of socialism at stake.

title: Recovery supported by international credit
text: American loans, German reparations, and Allied debt payments form a circular financial flow supporting a fragile recovery.

title: Germany joins the League of Nations
text: German membership forms part of the period of diplomatic stabilization described in the reading.
note: The reading describes membership without specifying its year; 1926 supplies the date for the timeline.

title: Guomindang forces take Shanghai and turn against Communists
text: The chronology table places this event within China’s postwar political upheaval.

title: NEP gives way to the First Five-Year Plan
text: The sidebar points toward Stalin’s program of rapid state-directed industrialization.

title: Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Union
text: Stalin’s victory over his rival accompanies the consolidation of personal and party power.

title: Great Depression ends the era of recovery
text: The final photographed page points forward to the collapse of the fragile postwar prosperity.

title: Israel is established
text: The Zionist handout looks beyond the WWI period to statehood and Palestinian displacement.
note: Later context from the handout, not an event during the 1919 negotiations.
